tools.name: get_offers
tools.description: Returns the three ways to start with Forwardsmith (Information Flow Mapping Session, FDE Build Sprint, FDE 30-60-90 engagement) with duration, starting price as a number in EUR excl. VAT, what it delivers, what is not included, the ownership statement and a list of things the site does not publish,

tools.name: get_approach
tools.description: Returns how a forward-deployed engineer of Forwardsmith works: Map, Build, Hand over; the five stations of the method and its golden rule; the six kinds of work; the eight points that belong in a statement of work; what must be ready before the start; and the handover test.

tools.name: check_fit
tools.description: Deterministic fit check with nine yes/no signals taken from the published article on when an FDE fits and when it does not. Returns one of: fits, start_with_mapping, not_clear_yet, wait, something_else_fits_better, each with the sentence from the site it is based on. It also says when another kind o

tools.name: run_readiness_scan
tools.description: Runs the same six-question FDE Readiness Scan as the page on forwardsmith.com, with the same scoring. Returns the score, the recommended starting point with its starting price, what is already in place and what to prepare. Indicative self-assessment, not a quote.

tools.name: scope_mapping_session
tools.description: Takes one process as 2-20 steps and returns per step whether it is handled by code (MCP/API), by a model (and on which route) or by a person, whether a redaction gate comes first and whether human approval is needed. tools.name: estimate_engagement
tools.description: Adds up the published starting prices for a chosen path of one to three steps (mapping, sprint, fde). Returns the lines, the sum as a lower bound in EUR excl. VAT, what is not included and what is not published. No discounts, no new prices, not a quote.

tools.name: prepare_intake_request
tools.description: Turns what you learned into a ready-to-send intake request: a brief in ten numbered lines, a link that opens the intake form with the message already filled in, and (once delivery to the inbox is confirmed) an e-mail to contact@forwardsmith.com. findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_offers · Private data: prepare_intake_request · Public sink: get_offers, get_approach, prepare_intake_request · Destructive: run_readiness_scan.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_offers · Private data: prepare_intake_request · Public sink: get_offers, get_approach, prepare_intake_request · Destructive: run_readiness_scan

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
